name: python
source: curated for hotdoc M2 (Python 3.14 command line and everyday language patterns)

entries.title: import statement
entries.syntax: import module, from module import name, from module import name as alias
entries.description: Load modules and functions to use in your program.

examples.code: import json as j; data = j.loads('{"key": "value"}'); print(data)

entries.title: if/elif/else conditional
entries.description: Execute different blocks of code based on conditions.

entries.title: for loop
entries.description: Iterate over sequences like lists, tuples, or strings.

entries.title: while loop
entries.description: Repeat block while condition is true; use break/continue to control flow.

entries.title: function definition
entries.description: Define reusable code blocks with parameters and return values.

entries.title: class definition
entries.description: Define objects with properties and methods using object-oriented programming.

entries.title: list comprehension
entries.syntax: [expression for item in iterable if condition]
entries.description: Create lists concisely by applying expressions to iterables.

examples.code:
numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
squares = [x**2 for x in numbers if x % 2 == 0]
print(squares)  # [4, 16]

entries.title: dictionary comprehension
entries.syntax: {key: value for item in iterable if condition}
entries.description: Create dictionaries concisely from iterables.

entries.title: try/except exception handling
entries.description: Catch and handle errors gracefully without crashing.

entries.title: with statement (context manager)
entries.description: Safely manage resources like files, automatically closing them.

examples.code:
with open("file.txt", "r") as f:
    content = f.read()
    print(content)

entries.title: lambda function
entries.description: Create small anonymous functions for quick operations.

examples.code:
numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4]
squared = list(map(lambda x: x**2, numbers))
print(squared)

entries.title: string formatting
entries.description: Insert variables into strings using f-strings or format methods.

examples.code:
name = "Alice"; age = 30
print(f"{name} is {age} years old and will be {age+1} next year")

entries.title: slicing sequences
entries.description: Extract portions of sequences like lists or strings.

examples.code:
text = "hello world"
print(text[0:5])      # hello
print(text[::2])      # hlowrd
print(text[::-1])     # dlrow olleh

entries.title: enumerate function
entries.description: Get both index and value when iterating over sequences.

entries.title: zip function
entries.syntax: for a, b in zip(iterable1, iterable2): ...
entries.description: Combine multiple iterables element-wise for parallel iteration.

examples.code:
names = ["Alice", "Bob"]
ages = [25, 30]
for name, age in zip(names, ages):
    print(f"{name}: {age}")

entries.title: Run subprocess
entries.description: Run another program and optionally capture its output.

examples.code:
import subprocess
result = subprocess.run(['git', 'status', '--short'], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True)
print(result.stdout)

entries.title: Run async main
entries.description: Run an async entry point and manage the event loop lifecycle.

examples.code:
import asyncio

async def main():
    await asyncio.sleep(1)

asyncio.run(main())
